comments.body:
## ROOT CAUSE — confirmed, reproduced deterministically on the first attempt

Not a capture race, not handler teardown, and NOT the `confirm_store is None` path this
ticket originally suspected. It is a **leaked logger LEVEL on the sibling `rebar_reconciler`
root**, which the suite's existing caplog containment guard does not cover.

### Mechanism

The two log lines in the failure differ only in LEVEL, and both fire on the same code path:

* per-item — `logger.warning(...)` in `_inbound_unlink_one`
  (`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py:578`)
* pass summary — `logger.info(...)` at the tail of `_inbound_update_apply_links`
  (same file, ~line 790)

Both use `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` = `rebar_reconciler.apply_inbound_records`.

`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/__main__.py:606` calls
`install_stderr_handler("rebar_reconciler")`, and `src/rebar/_logging.py:88` does
`logger.setLevel(level)` — pinning the shared **`rebar_reconciler`** logger to WARNING.
Loggers are process-global singletons and nothing restores it, so the first test in an xdist
worker that drives the reconciler entrypoint in-process poisons every later test in that
worker.

`caplog.at_level(logging.INFO)` **cannot** rescue this: with no `logger=` argument it raises
the ROOT logger's level, not the intermediate `rebar_reconciler` logger's. The INFO record is
therefore dropped by `isEnabledFor` at the originating logger, before any handler is
consulted, while the WARNING record still propagates to caplog's root handler. That is
exactly the observed asymmetry — summary missing, per-item line present — and it explains why
`confirm_store` was never the culprit (if it had been `None`, the per-item WARNING would have
been missing too, since that line is emitted only when the store is non-None).

### Why the existing guard missed it

The repo already documents this exact vector and already contains it: `tests/_log_integrity.py`
(`current_level` / `restore_level`) plus the autouse `_rebar_log_propagation_guard` in
`tests/conftest.py`. But both are hard-coded to a single root,
`REBAR_LOGGER_NAME = "rebar"` — while `src/rebar/_logging.py`'s own module docstring names
**two** shared roots ("the sibling `rebar_reconciler` root for the reconciler subprocess,
which is imported top-level as `rebar_reconciler.*`"). Everything under `rebar_reconciler.*`
was simply outside the containment.

### Named polluter + reproduction (AC1, RED)

```
pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/orchestrate/test_main_entry.py \
       tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_inbound_removal_confirmation_a4bd.py \
       -p no:randomly
=> 1 failed, 15 passed
AssertionError: ['_apply_inbound_update: declining the inbound removal of blocks link ...']
```

Deterministic, first try — the identical assertion text CI reported. `test_main_entry.py` is
one instance, not the unique one: any test that reaches the reconciler `main()` in-process
does it, which is why worksteal made shard/run selection look random.

### AC4 — is the `declined` count a production defect?

**No, correct by design.** In `_inbound_update_apply_links` the counter increments only under
`elif confirm_store is not None and not confirm_store.is_confirmed(...)`. When the store is
`None` the confirmation guard in `_inbound_unlink_one` is bypassed entirely, so the removal is
**applied**, not declined — there is nothing to report and `declined == 0` is truthful, not
an under-report. The summary is suppressed because no decline happened. No production
logging behaviour is changed by this fix.

comments.body:
THIRD OCCURRENCE, and a detail that narrows the mechanism — 2026-08-13, `macos-latest py3.13` shard only, every ubuntu shard green each time.

Occurrences today:
1. Gerrit **1715** (event_append split; `src/rebar/_store/` only) — run 31680986340.
2. Gerrit **1716** (rich-text conflict-safety pins, story `disparaged-parodistic-shrew`; TESTS-ONLY, one new file) — run 31681638153.
3. Gerrit **1716** again, after a recheck — run 31683437250.

All three: `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_inbound_removal_confirmation_a4bd.py::test_pass_summary_reports_the_decline_count`, failing at
`assert any("declined 1 inbound link removal" in m for m in messages)`.

**The narrowing detail: the captured records are not EMPTY — they contain the per-link decline line, and only the pass-SUMMARY line is missing.** In run 1 the captured line named link `1bc5-25e4-0ebd-44e0 -> e727-b3b4-02ff-4972`; in run 3 it named `dd93-74a0-7669-4b1e -> 5d49-b6b2-1725-4a23`. Different ids across runs, same shape.

Two things follow:
- The capture is LIVE and working when the per-link record is emitted, so this is not a caplog handler that was never attached. Something happens between the per-link emission and the later summary emission — a propagation/handler swap, or the summary being emitted under a different logger or after the fixture's capture scope ends.
- The differing link ids show the test body genuinely re-runs with fresh data each time, so the failure is not a stale-state artifact; it is ordering or timing.

Recheck is NOT being attempted a fourth time on 1716 per operator instruction — it will be rebased over the fix once this lands. Flagging that this is now blocking a change that cannot possibly reach the assertion (1716 adds one test file and touches no production code), so the flake is costing throughput on unrelated lanes, not just noise.

comments.body:
## Falsifying the `confirm_store is None` hypothesis (AC4, empirically)

A parallel reading of the code suggested the flake might be the test intermittently taking
the storeless path, making the missing summary CORRECT and pointing at a production
under-count. That is ruled out, and the evidence is in this module already.

**The per-item line only exists on the storeful path.** In `_inbound_unlink_one`
(`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py:575-585`) the
"declining the inbound removal of ..." WARNING is emitted inside
`if confirm_store is not None and not confirm_store.is_confirmed(...)`. Its presence in the
failing capture is therefore positive proof that `confirm_store` was NOT None in the failing
run. The two candidate mechanisms are mutually exclusive and the log itself discriminates
between them.

**And a storeless pass produces no decline at all.** With no store the guard is bypassed and
the removal is APPLIED. That is already pinned by the sibling test in this very module,
`test_unopenable_store_declines_nothing`, which patches `_open_peer_confirmation_store` to
return `None` and asserts `applied == 1` and the link is gone. So the storeless path emits
NEITHER line — not the per-item one and not the summary — which is not the observed failure
shape.

**So `declined == 0` when the store is None is truthful, not an under-report:** nothing was
declined, because the removal went through. There is no production defect here and no
production logging behaviour is changed by this fix.

Final confirmation is behavioural, not argumentative: the fix touches only the test-side
logger-level containment and turns the deterministic reproduction from RED (1 failed, 15
passed) to GREEN (16 passed). If the mechanism had been storeless-path selection, a change to
`tests/_log_integrity.py` could not have altered the outcome.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_inbound_removal_confirmation_a4bd.py::test_pass_summary_reports_the_decline_count`
fails intermittently under CI's `-n 3 --dist worksteal` invocation (it -1'd Gerrit 1715 and
1716 in one hour, on both macOS and ubuntu shards) and passes 10/10 in isolation. The
assertion wants the SUMMARY line `declined 1 inbound link removal`; `caplog` holds only the
PER-ITEM line `declining the inbound removal of ...`.

**Root cause (reproduced deterministically, not a hypothesis).** The two lines differ in
LEVEL, not in code path: the per-item decline is `logger.warning` in
`apply_inbound_records._inbound_unlink_one`, the pass summary is `logger.info` at the end of
`apply_inbound_records._inbound_update_apply_links`. Both fire; only the INFO one can be
dropped. Both use `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` =
`rebar_reconciler.apply_inbound_records`.

`rebar_reconciler/__main__.py:606` calls `install_stderr_handler("rebar_reconciler")`, and
`rebar/_logging.py:88` does `logger.setLevel(level)` — pinning the shared
**`rebar_reconciler`** root logger to WARNING, process-globally and never restored. Any test
that drives the reconciler entrypoint in-process (e.g.
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/orchestrate/test_main_entry.py`) leaks that level to every later
test in the same xdist worker. `caplog.at_level(logging.INFO)` with no `logger=` argument
raises the **ROOT** level only, so the INFO record is discarded at the originating logger by
`isEnabledFor` before any handler is consulted — while the WARNING record still arrives.
That is exactly the observed asymmetry.

The repo already documents this precise vector and already contains containment for it —
`tests/_log_integrity.py` (`restore_level`) plus the autouse
`_rebar_log_propagation_guard` in `tests/conftest.py` — but both are hard-coded to the single
root `REBAR_LOGGER_NAME = "rebar"`. `rebar/_logging.py`'s own docstring names **two** shared
roots ("the sibling `rebar_reconciler` root for the reconciler subprocess"). The guard simply
misses the sibling, so reconciler-side INFO assertions are unprotected.

Confirmed RED locally, first try, deterministic:
`pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/orchestrate/test_main_entry.py tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_inbound_removal_confirmation_a4bd.py -p no:randomly`
=> 1 failed, 15 passed, with the exact CI assertion text.

This is a TEST-INFRASTRUCTURE defect, not a production one: when the confirmation store is
`None` the removal is not declined at all (it proceeds), so `declined == 0` and a suppressed
summary is correct-by-design. No production logging change is warranted.

## Approach

Generalise the existing caplog coverage-integrity guard from one shared root to the set of
shared roots, rather than papering over the symptom with a `logger=` argument on the one
assertion. The mechanism is process-global and generic — every `rebar_reconciler.*` INFO/DEBUG
assertion in the suite is exposed to it — so containment at the guard is the fix that closes
the class; a per-test tweak would leave the next such assertion to flake.

In `tests/_log_integrity.py`, replace the scalar `REBAR_LOGGER_NAME` with
`SHARED_LOGGER_NAMES = ("rebar", "rebar_reconciler")` and make the four primitives operate
over that tuple: `propagation_failure` reports the first non-propagating root by name,
`restore_propagation` re-enables all of them, `current_level` returns a
`dict[str, int]` snapshot, and `restore_level` takes that snapshot and reports whether any
root moved. The `tests/conftest.py` autouse fixture keeps its exact shape (snapshot at setup,
restore in `finally`); only the value it carries becomes a mapping. Rationale for the tuple
over per-test opt-in: the leak is caused by legitimate code (a real entrypoint installing its
handler), so containment — every test starting from the same level — is what makes log
assertions order-independent, which is the property CI needs.

## Scope

- `tests/_log_integrity.py` — multi-root primitives + docstring naming the reconciler root.
- `tests/conftest.py` — the autouse guard carries the per-root level snapshot.
- `tests/unit/test_caplog_coverage_integrity.py` — update the self-tests to the new signature
  and add a pytester pair proving the `rebar_reconciler` root is contained (without the guard
  a leaked reconciler level breaks a later INFO assertion; with it, green).

No `src/` change.

## Testing

- **Failure path first (the reproduction).** Run the polluter module and the flaky module in
  one process with `-p no:randomly`; assert it goes from 1-failed to 0-failed with the fix.
- **Guard self-test, both directions (pytester, in
  `tests/unit/test_caplog_coverage_integrity.py`).** New pair mirroring the existing `rebar`
  level pair, but poisoning `logging.getLogger("rebar_reconciler").setLevel(WARNING)` and then
  asserting an INFO record from `rebar_reconciler.probe`: WITHOUT the guard conftest the later
  test FAILS; WITH it, both pass. Worked example of the poisoned file:
  `def test_poisoner(): logging.getLogger("rebar_reconciler").setLevel(logging.WARNING)`
  followed by `def test_info(caplog):` doing `with caplog.at_level(logging.INFO):
  logging.getLogger("rebar_reconciler.probe").info("hello")` and
  `assert any("hello" in r.getMessage() for r in caplog.records)`.
- **Edge/no-op path.** `restore_level` on an unmoved snapshot returns `False`; a snapshot
  where only one root moved returns `True` and restores just that root.
- **Propagation vector unchanged.** The existing propagation self-tests keep passing, and a
  new case asserts a non-propagating `rebar_reconciler` root is also blamed by name.
- **CI invocation.** The enclosing module plus the reconciler subtree under
  `-n 3 --dist worksteal`, repeated, plus the full CI selection.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The order dependency is named and demonstrated: a two-module invocation
      (`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/orchestrate/test_main_entry.py` then the a4bd module,
      `-p no:randomly`) fails BEFORE the change and passes after — both runs recorded on this
      ticket.
- [x] `tests/_log_integrity.py` exposes `SHARED_LOGGER_NAMES` containing both `"rebar"` and
      `"rebar_reconciler"`, and `tests/conftest.py`'s autouse guard restores the level of both
      — verified by the new pytester self-test pair going red without the guard and green with
      it (`pytest tests/unit/test_caplog_coverage_integrity.py`, all pass).
- [x] `pytest -m "not integration and not external" -n 3 --dist worksteal --timeout=300` passes
      on the change, and the a4bd module passes across 10 consecutive
      `-n 3 --dist worksteal` runs of `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/` (run count recorded in a
      ticket comment).
- [x] The `confirm_store is None` question is answered in a ticket comment with the code
      citation: it is correct-by-design (no store => no decline => `declined == 0`), and NOT
      the mechanism behind this flake, so no production logging change is made.

the autouse containment fixture snapshots and restores the level of both shared roots
self-tests updated to the multi-root signature plus a pytester pair proving the reconciler root is contained
